la:verb:pereo.gloss: to perish, pass away, die, be ruined
senses: to perish, pass away, die, be ruined
to vanish, disappear, come to nothing
la:verb:pereo.html:
pĕr-ĕo, ĭi (īvi), ĭtum, īre (periet for peribit, Coripp. Johann. 7, 27;
perf. perivit, : perīt,: perisset,: perisse,; ; fut. periet, ), v. n.
To pass away, come to nothing; to vanish, disappear, be lost: e patriā,: ecqua inde perisset soror,: ne vena periret aquae,.—
Esp., to pass through, leak, be absorbed (poet.): lymphae Dolium pereuntis,; cf.: postremo pereunt imbres, ubi eos pater aether In gremium matris terrai praecipitavit,.—
To pass away, to be destroyed, to perish (the predom. and class. signif. of the word; syn.: occĭdo, intereo, obeo).
In gen.: aedes cum fundamento perierint,: tantam pecuniam tam brevi tempore perire potuisse,: totum exercitum periturum,: fac pereat vitreo miles ab hoste tuus (in the game of chess),let your knight be taken by a pawn,: causae cur urbes perirent,: peritura regna,: puppis,: Troja peritura,: pereunt sole tepente nives,melt away,: telum rubigine,: comae,: fabae laeso flore,.—Of the crocus: gaudet calcari et atteri, pereundoque melius provenit,.—
In partic.
To perish, lose one's life, die (class.): non intellego, quamobrem, si vivere honeste non possunt, perire turpiter velint; aut cur minore dolore perituros se cum multis, quam si soli pereant, arbitrentur,: summo cruciatu supplicioque,: fame,: eodem leto esse pereundum,: morbo,: naufragio,: hominum manibus,: uterque juravit, periturum inter nos secretum,that it should perish with us,: ab Hannibale,at his hands,: perire turpiter,: fortiter,: generosius,: a morbo,.—
To pine away with love, to be desperately in love; to love to desperation (poet.): indigno cum Gallus amore peribat,; : quo beatus Vulnere, quā pereat sagittā,: ipse Paris nudā fertur periisse Lacaenā,.—With acc. of the beloved object, .—
To be lost, wasted, spent in vain: ne et oleum et opera perierit,: tempora,: labor,: nullus perit otio dies,: ne nummi pereant,: minae,: aurum,; cf. actiones,.—
To be lost, ruined, undone: quid fieri tum potuit? jampridem perieramus,: meo vitio pereo,.—Hence, perii, etc., as an exclamation of despair, I am lost! I'm undone! hei mihi, disperii! vocis non habeo satis: vicini, interii, perii,: perii, interii, occidi! quo curram! quo non curram?: perii animo,am disheartened,; cf.: ingenio perii,; : periimus, actum est,we are lost, it is all over with us,: perierat et inventus est,; .—So, peream, si, nisi, in asseverations, may I perish, may I die, if or if not, ; Cassiod. ap. ; ; .—Gerund and gerundive: nisi illud perdo argentum, pereundum est mihi,; : pereundi figurae,: pereundi terminus,: puppis pereunda est probe,must be lost,.—
Trop., of moral qualities, etc.: pudor periit,: fides,: virtus,.

la:noun:peregrinatio.gloss: travel, travel abroad, journey, stay in a foreign place
senses: travel, travel abroad, journey, stay in a foreign place
la:noun:peregrinatio.html:
pĕrĕgrīnātĭo, ōnis, f.
peregrinor
,
a being or living abroad, a sojourning, a travelling in foreign parts, a travelling about, travel, peregrination (class.).
Lit.: perpetua,: transmarina,; ; ; : terra peregrinationis tuae,: tempus in peregrinatione consumere,.—In plur., .—
Transf., of animals: bestiae peregrinatione laetantur,.—Of muscles, .

la:adv:perendie.html:
pĕrendĭē, adv.
Gr. πέραν-dies
,
on the day after to-morrow (class.): cras agito, perendie agito,; ; : scies igitur fortasse cras, summum perendie,; .

la:adj:perexiguus.html:
pĕr-exĭgŭus, a, um, adj.,
very small, very little (class.): semen perexiguum,: dies,very short,: et perminuta bona corporis,: loci spatium,: argentum,: ignes,: frumentum,.—Adv.: pĕrexĭgŭē, very little, very sparingly: perexigue et γλίσχρως praebere, .

la:adj:perennis.html:
pĕrennis († pĕremnis, Inscr. Ann. p. Chr. 341 ap. Guattani Monum. Inedit. 1, 5, p. 39), e (
abl. sing. perenne, ; ), adj.
per-annus
, that lasts or continues the year through (post-Aug.): aves perennes,that remain with us all the year round,.—
Transf., everlasting, never failing, unceasing, perpetual, perennial (class.; cf.: jugis, perpetuus): aquae,; cf. : fons,: amnis,: rivi,: cursus stellarum,: vinum,i. e. that bears keeping,: adamas,: monumenta,; of a person: super Astra ferar,.—Comp.: exegi monumentum aere perennius,more lasting, more enduring,.—
Trop., unfailing, uninterrupted, continual, perpetual, etc.: lucrum,: perennis et contestata majorum virtus,: continuata motio et perennis,: loquacitas,: animus in rem publicam,.—Hence, adv., in two forms, pĕrenne (post-Aug.) and pĕrennĭter (post-class.).
pĕrenne.
Lit., all the year through, .—
Transf., constantly, perpetually (postclass.): abies perenne durabilis,, 1: perenne vivax,.—
pĕrennĭter, constantly, continually, always, perpetually: arbor frondens perenniter,: perenniter servare amicitias,; Cod. Th. 7, 20, 2; .

la:verb:pererro.gloss: to wander through, roam or ramble over
senses: to wander through, roam or ramble over
la:verb:pererro.html:
pĕr-erro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to wander through, to roam or ramble over (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: fallacem circum vespertinumque pererro Saepe forum,: locum,: freta,: saltus et fontes,: orbem, Col. praef. 1: cellas,: reges,to roam about from one king to another, § 6.— Pass.: arva pererrantur Peligna,: pererratus orbis,; cf.: pererrato ponto,.—
Transf.: totumque pererrat Luminibus tacitis,surveys all over,: sonus pererrat cornua, i. e. errat per tubam,.

la:verb:peredo.html:
pĕr-ĕdo, ēdi, ēsum, 3, v. a.,
to eat up, consume (poet.).
Lit.: cibum, Plaut. Fragm. ap. P.: quinque panes et gemellos pisces,.—
Transf., to consume, devour, etc.: nec peredit Impositam celer ignis Aetnam,: lacrimae peredere umore exsangues genas, old poet in (Trag. Rel. p. 225 Rib.): vesco sale saxa peresa,: saxa, (18): morbo peresa Vellera,. —
Trop., to consume, waste away, etc.: quos durus amor crudeli tabe peredit, : languoribus peresus,.

la:adj:peregrinus.html:
pĕrĕgrīnus, a, um, adj.
peregre
,
that comes from foreign parts, strange, foreign, exotic (cf.: exter, externus).
Lit.
In gen.
Adj.: ad portum mittunt servulos, ancillulas: peregrina navis, etc.,: facies,: homo,: mulier,: caelum,: amnes,: arbores,: aves,: morbus,: eluamus hodie peregrina omnia, (668 Ritschl): labor,i. e. of travelling,: amores,for foreign women,: fasti,of foreign nations,: divitiae,: mores,: terror,of a foreign enemy,: velut peregrinum otium alicui permittere,almost the leisure of a stranger,: peregrina sacra appellantur, quae coluntur eorum more, a quibus sunt accepta, Müll.—
Subst.: pĕrĕgrīnus, i, m., a foreigner, stranger (very freq. and class.; syn.: hospes, advena, alienigena; opp. civis): peregrinus ego sum,: peregrini atque advenae,: peregrini et incolae officium est,: peregrini reges,: ne in nostrā patriā peregrini atque advenae esse videamur,.—
pĕrĕgrīna, ae, f., a foreign woman (poet.), ; .—
Subst., in partic., opp. to a Roman citizen, a foreign resident, an alien: neque civem, neque peregrinum,: peregrinus fit is, cui aquā et igni interdictum est, Regul. tit. 11; .—
As adj.: praetor,who decided causes between foreign residents,; cf. ; : peregrinus ager est, qui neque Romanus, neque hosticus habetur, Müll.; cf.: agrorum sunt genera quinque, Romanus, Gabinus, peregrinus, hosticus, incertus, etc., Müll.: peregrini milites,Roman troops who were not Roman citizens,; their quarters in Rome were called, after them, CASTRA PEREGRINA, and were situated in the second region, by the modern S. Stefano Rotondo, ; cf. Marin. Atti dei Frat. Arv. p. 434 sq.: provincia,.—
Trop., strange, raw, inexperienced (class.): nullā in re tironem ac rudem, nec peregrinum atque hospitem in agendo esse,; .

la:verb:peregrinor.gloss: to be or live in foreign parts, be abroad or a stranger, go abroad, travel about; roam, rove; sojourn abroad, peregrinate
senses: to be or live in foreign parts, be abroad or a stranger, go abroad, travel about; roam, rove; sojourn abroad, peregrinate
la:verb:peregrinor.html:
pĕrĕgrīnor, ātus, 1,
v. dep. n. [id.], to be or live in foreign parts, to sojourn abroad, to travel about (class.; cf.: peragro, migro).
Lit.: peregrinari totā Asiā,: in alienā civitate,: in terrā,. —
Trop.
To go abroad, to travel about; to roam, rove, or wander about: haec studia pernoctant nobiscum, peregrinantur, rusticantur,: animus late longeque peregrinatur, : in infinitatem omnem,to roam through all infinity,.—
To be abroad, be a stranger, a sojourner (cf. peregrinus, B.): philosophiae quasi civitatem dare, quae quidem adhuc peregrinari Romae videbatur,: vestrae peregrinantur aures?.—With ab, to be absent from, a stranger to: a corpore, a Dei regno,, Serm. 12, § 17; id. de Isaac et An. 5, 17; so, a Domino,; cf. .

senses: to last for many years, to last, continue, endure
la:verb:perenno.html:
pĕrenno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
id.
.
Act., to keep or preserve long (post-Aug.): ea res, etiamsi non in totum perennat, certe usque in alteram vindemiam plerumque vini saporem servat, (dub.; al. perennem); 12, 19, 2.—
Neutr., to last for many years, to last, continue, endure (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): arte perennat amor,: ut diutius perennent boves,; : domus,: gens ultra aevi nostri terminos perennans,.

, to ride through, ride hither and thither, ride about; to drive about (class. but not in Cic.).
Neutr.: inter duas acies perequitans,: longe ex viā,: per omnes partes,to drive about,.—
Act.: aciem,: puer delphino maria perequitans,.

la:adj:perendinus.html:
pĕrendĭnus, a, um, adj.
perendie
,
after to-morrow (class.): tot homines tam ingeniosos, per tot annos statuere non potuisse, utrum diem tertium, an perendinum dici oporteret,: perendino die,.—Absol. (anteand post-class.): tu in perendinum paratus sis,against the day after to-morrow,: dies perendini,.

la:adj:perelegans.html:
pĕr-ēlĕgans, antis, adj.,
very neat, fine, or elegant (class.): genus,: oratio,: ingenium,.—Adv.: pĕr-ēlĕganter, very finely, very elegantly: pereleganter dicere,.

la:adj:perexcelsus.html:
pĕr-excelsus, a, um,
very high, lofty: Henna, ubi ea gesta esse memorantur, est loco perexcelso,.
